title: delta-aware-batcher-and-cost-mapper-with-conservative-quant-profiles
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Adds a delta-aware batch allocator (reduces wasted padding and KV cache churn) and a tenant-scoped cost-mapper plus conservative quantization profiles. Expected ~12% p50 token-cost reduction on conversational workloads and safer fallbacks for long-tail tenants.
description:
Motivation: Many workloads show high variance in request sequence lengths and prefix reuse. Conservative global batching wastes tokens and KV cache bandwidth for tenants with high delta (length variance) or highly prefix-skewed traffic. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a delta-aware batch allocator that groups requests by effective delta (new tokens beyond shared prefix) and prefers compact micro-batches when delta is small, and 2) a tenant-scoped cost-mapper that synthesizes a recommended quantization profile and batch sizing defaults based on observed p50/p95 token-cost and end-to-end latency targets. The goal is automated, low-risk defaults that improve unit economics without sacrificing SLOs.

What changed (high-level):
- runtime/batcher/delta_allocator.py: new allocator that calculates an "effective delta" heuristic and exposes a BatchHint API consumed by the scheduler. The allocator supports fallthrough to existing continuous-batch logic.
- runtime/quant/profiles/conservative_delta.yaml: new conservative quant profiles (4-bit fallback ladders) tuned for small models and long-tail tenant safety.
- tools/cost-mapper/mapper.go: lightweight CLI and service used by onboarding to generate suggested tenant defaults from recent traces.
- console/frontend/src/components/CostDefaultsEditor.tsx: UI to preview and accept generated defaults per-tenant.
- docs/runbooks/cost-mapper.md: operator runbook and safe-rollback steps.
- tests/test_delta_allocator.py and tests/test_cost_mapper_integration.py: unit & integration tests and small synthetic workloads used in CI.

Design notes: The allocator computes delta = request_total_tokens - longest_common_prefix_tokens across a micro-batch window; it then assigns a batch weight proportional to delta_quantile (empirically we found Q=0.6 works well) to avoid forcing large batches when delta is low. BatchHint includes target_batch_size and max_wait_ms; the scheduler respects these hints but keeps global SLO overrides. The cost-mapper runs offline over a 24h window (default) and outputs a safe quantization ladder plus batch/cache defaults; it marks recommendations as "conservative" or "aggressive" depending on observed p95 latency headroom. Recommendations are surfaced in the Console and can be applied with a single click.

Config example (default conservative output) :
```yaml
tenant: tenant-acme
recommended_batch_size: 8
recommended_max_wait_ms: 25
quant_profile: conservative-delta-4bit
notes: "Conservative defaults: prioritize SLOs, preserve KV cache reuse, fall back to float16 if regression detected."
```

Backwards compatibility & rollout: The allocator is additive and off by default; we wire a feature-flag (runtime.features.delta_batching) and a tenant opt-in. Cost-mapper only produces suggestions; it does not change serving configs without explicit acceptance. Default behavior continues to use existing continuous-batch allocator unless the feature flag is enabled or the tenant accepts the suggested defaults from Console.

Testing & benchmarks: CI runs unit tests and a small end-to-end scenario that simulates 5000 requests with mixed prefix reuse. Benchmarks on our perf-canary fleet show a ~12% reduction in p50 token-cost and a small improvement in cold-start throughput for the sample conversational workload. We included a smoke policy that ensures p95 latency does not regress more than 5% for any tenant in the candidate set.

Risks & mitigations: Quantization profiles are conservative and include an automatic rollback detector (regression alerts tied to prompt sets). The allocator respects global SLO overrides and has a safety cap on micro-batch rate to avoid undue scheduler churn. Operator runbook included for quick rollback.

Related work: This complements earlier autoscaling and prefill optimizations but focuses on reducing wasted compute from padding and unnecessary KV cache thrash for variable-length conversational workloads.

Checklist:

- [x] Conservative quant profiles and ladder
- [x] Cost-mapper tool + CLI
- [x] Console UI for accepting defaults
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Runbook and rollback instructions

Merging notes: Squash-merged; post-merge steps include enabling the feature-flag in canary for two tenants and monitoring the regression alert dashboard for 48h.
